The test image shows a tomato plant that has completely collapsed. Key features:
- Stem lying horizontal with a prominent tan/pale canker-like lesion
- All leaves brown, wilted, and dead
- Stem collapse appears at a node/junction
- Black plastic mulch in background (field/greenhouse production)

This pattern of stem rot causing plant collapse narrows candidates to: Southern_Blight, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, and Phytophthora_Blight. Let me view one reference from each.

Analyzing all four references against the test image:

- **Southern Blight**: Shows white cottony mycelium at soil line — not present in test image
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Black sclerotia on/in stem — the test stem shows tan/bleached coloration with possible dark spots, consistent with Sclerotinia stem rot
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Shows leaf yellowing/marginal necrosis — doesn't match the stem collapse pattern
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Shows dark brown/black water-soaked streaking lesions — test stem is more pale/tan than dark

The test image shows a complete plant collapse with a **pale/bleached tan stem** lying horizontal — the hallmark of Sclerotinia white mold (timber rot), which bleaches stem tissue and causes collapse. The dark spot visible on the stem could be a sclerotium embedded in the cortex.
